Independent MP Rupert Lowe launches Restore Britain, positioning it as a hardline response to mass immigration and what supporters describe as national decline. Promising to reverse illegal migration and detain and deport those without status, the movement has rapidly attracted tens of thousands of members — while critics argue some proposals cross legal and moral boundaries. The debate now spans mass deportations, grooming gang accountability, digital ID, cultural nationalism, and whether Britain’s political duopoly is fracturing. Beneath it all sits a deeper question: is this reform, reaction — or the start of a wider political realignment?
